Scholarship overview

Bristol’s Health and Life Sciences PGR scholarships fund advertised doctoral projects across biomedical, biological, psychological and health research. Both UK and non-UK applicants may apply.

Research Areas

  • Health and life sciences
  • Biology
  • Psychology
  • Neuroscience

Funding and duration

ComponentDetails
FundingFull UK/non-UK tuition waiver; GBP 2,100/year research costs.
MaintenanceUKRI outside-London rate
Duration4 years; September 2027 start

Eligibility and Requirements

UK and International candidates meeting the project/programme entry criteria and demonstrating research fit. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
Recruitment2027 project guidance available
DeadlineDeadline specified for the chosen funded project

How to Apply

Search funded projects using “University of Bristol Scholarship”, contact supervisors and apply online. Submit a separate application for each choice; maximum two projects.

Provide a two-page CV and project-specific personal statement. Visa, IHS and relocation costs are excluded.

About University of Bristol

The University of Bristol offers doctoral research in health and life sciences, including biomedical science, psychology, neuroscience and biological science. Its funded project routes combine supervision with research training, and applicants choose projects that match their preparation and interests.

Official details: Programme information

Application route: Application form or official instructions

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
